context: Each of the three rows uses five nodes arranged as 1, 3, 2, 5, 4. Read from top to bottom to compare the three ways of linking them.

frames.explanation: A singly linked list can be traversed only toward the successor. Any node in a circular linked list can serve as the head. A doubly linked list supports traversal in either direction using next or prev, at the cost of storing an extra reference to the predecessor.
frames.title: Three common types of linked lists

summary: The same five nodes, 1, 3, 2, 5, and 4, illustrate how links differ in singly linked, circular, and doubly linked lists.

tables.caption: References and endpoints in three types of linked lists
rows: The next reference of tail node 4 points to None
A line below the list links tail node 4 back to node 1, closing the loop
The nodes appear in the order 1, 3, 2, 5, 4. Between each adjacent pair, next points right to the successor and prev points left to the predecessor
Node 1's prev points to None on the left, and node 4's next points to None on the right
